meta.title: Seasons Around the World — Set 3
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Hemispheres and details fact-check quiz for 'Seasons Around the World'.

questions.question: Near the North Pole, when does the sun never shine?
questions.explanation: The text says: 'Near the North Pole, the sun never shines in winter. It is dark all day!'

questions.question: In summer, the sun never sets in Antarctica.
questions.explanation: True. In summer, the sun stays in the sky all day and night in Antarctica.

questions.question: Which place is the coldest place on Earth?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth. It never gets warm, even in summer.

questions.question: In fall, the days start to get longer again.
questions.explanation: False. The text says: 'During fall, the days start to get shorter again.'

questions.question: How many seasons are there in some tropical parts of the world?
questions.explanation: In some parts of the world, there are only two seasons: a rainy season and a dry season.

questions.question: Near the equator, the seasons do not _______ much.
questions.explanation: The weather remains very similar all year long near the equator, so seasons don't change much.

questions.question: Why do some butterflies travel from the United States to Mexico in the fall?
options: To find more food to store.
To see the fall colors of the leaves.
To build nests in the trees.
questions.explanation: Butterflies travel south to Mexico in the fall so they can stay warm during the cold winter months.

questions.question: Sort these features based on whether they describe the Equator or Antarctica:
items: The sun never sets in summer
It is the coldest place on Earth

categories.label: Antarctica Features
answers: The sun never sets in summer
It is the coldest place on Earth

questions.explanation: The equator has very little seasonal change. Antarctica has a midnight sun in summer and is extremely cold.

questions.question: Most plants and trees stop growing in winter, and some die.
questions.explanation: True. The cold temperature and lack of sunlight cause plants to stop growing or die in winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe winter days:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'In winter days are shorter.' This means we have less daylight hours.

questions.question: What happens to the daylight hours in summer?
options: The days stay the same as winter.
questions.explanation: The text says: 'During summer, the days are longer than they are during other seasons.'

questions.question: In fall, many birds and animals move to warmer places where they can find _______.
questions.hint: What living things eat to survive.
questions.explanation: Animals move to warmer places in autumn because it is easier to find food there during winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show seasons near the equator:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Seasons don't change much near the equator.' The weather is hot all year round.

questions.question: In summer, Antarctica gets very warm because the sun never sets.
questions.explanation: False. The text says: 'Even in summer, it never gets warm here' in Antarctica.

questions.question: During spring, what helps plants grow?
questions.explanation: The spring section says: 'The rain and warmer weather help plants grow.'
